obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card compromise (Hotels merchant accounts, Acquirer A)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25) Section A.3.1; merchant agreement (fictional term)
trigger: Reasonable suspicion of unauthorized access to card data or a payment system at the 30 owned or leased hotels
deadline: Immediately (WTDIC A.3.1); merchant agreement: within 24 hours of suspicion (fictional)
notify: Acquirer A
notifying_entity: Hotels (Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance)

obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card compromise (Attractions, Acquirer B)
citation: Visa WTDIC v10.0 Section A.3.1; merchant agreement (fictional term)
trigger: Reasonable suspicion of compromise of park POS or kiosks
deadline: Immediately; merchant agreement: within 24 hours of suspicion (fictional)
notify: Acquirer B
notifying_entity: Attractions (Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance)

obligation: Acquirer notice (Vacation Ownership, Acquirer C)
citation: Visa WTDIC v10.0 Section A.3.1; merchant agreement (fictional term)
trigger: Suspicion that Vacation Ownership card systems are affected
deadline: Immediately if affected
notify: Acquirer C
applies_at_this_tier: Only if gallery or owner portal card systems are affected (not in this scenario: owner portal payments use SYS-G4, which was not compromised)
notifying_entity: Vacation Ownership (Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance)

obligation: Visa notification of a compromise event
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a payment system; applies to merchants and service providers
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations, normally through each acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Hotels (merchant and service provider) and Attractions
notifying_entity: Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Visa incident report
citation: Visa WTDIC v10.0 Section A.2.1 and Attachment A
trigger: After notifying Visa
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa
notify: Visa and the acquirer, including containment and remediation steps with dates
notifying_entity: Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Visa at-risk account numbers
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
deadline: Within 3 calendar days
notify: Visa, through the acquirer's upload tools
notifying_entity: Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: PCI Forensic Investigator (if Visa requires one)
citation: Visa WTDIC v10.0 Sections A.5.1 and A.5.3
trigger: Formal notice from Visa requiring a PFI investigation
deadline: Contract a PFI within 5 business days; preliminary report within 5 business days of contracting; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation
notify: Visa and the affected acquirers. The PFI may not be the group's QSA firm or another firm that served the group as listed in A.5.3
notifying_entity: Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Other card brands (Mastercard, American Express, Discover)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of that brand's account data
deadline: Per each brand's rules; timing not verified here. Follow each acquirer's instructions and treat 24 hours as the working target
notify: Brand, normally through the acquirer
notifying_entity: Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: Notice to the payment system vendor
trigger: The incident involves a vulnerability in the payment processing system
deadline: Immediately (recommended); in this scenario the vendor is the entry point, so notice is coordinated with containment
notify: Legacy POS vendor (and the cloud POS, PMS, and P2PE providers for scoping)

obligation: Owner notice for managed hotels (merchants of record)
citation: Management agreements (fictional terms): agreements signed since 2020 require notice within 24 hours of suspicion; 31 pre-2020 agreements are silent
trigger: Suspected compromise of systems the Hotels division operates for an owner, or of data the division holds for an owner
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion for all owners as group practice (POL-03 4.4), whatever the agreement says
notify: Each affected ownership group (11 groups, 15 hotels in this scenario), with facts for the owner's acquirer notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and as service provider (PCI DSS 12.9)
notifying_entity: Hotels senior vice president of owner relations

obligation: Owners' acquirer notices (managed hotels)
citation: Owners' merchant agreements; Visa WTDIC v10.0 Section A.3.1
trigger: Owner informed by the division
deadline: Per each owner's merchant agreement; Visa's 3-day clock still applies to the compromise event
notify: Each owner's acquirer (the division prepares the facts and joins calls)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - owners are the merchants of record
notifying_entity: Each owner, supported by the Group Director of Payments and PCI Compliance

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers (unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise; 314.2)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery; discovery is the first day known to any employee, officer, or other agent (314.4(j)(2)), which includes the group SOC
notify: FTC, by the online form at ftc.gov, with the content listed in 314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - owners' bank account data of finance subsidiary loan customers was read from the guest profile hub (about 151,000 consumers)

obligation: FTC notice law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official provides a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Include in the FTC notice; initial delay up to 30 days, extendable up to 60 more days on written request
notify: FTC

obligation: Owners' association notice
citation: Association management agreements (fictional term: within 5 business days)
trigger: Maintenance-fee autopay bank data of association members was accessed
deadline: Within 5 business days of suspicion (fictional)
notify: Boards of the affected owners' associations (24)
notifying_entity: Vacation Ownership vice president of association management

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary: identity document numbers, financial account numbers, card numbers with codes, biometric data, credentials)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected guests, visitors, and owners reside
notifying_entity: Each affected entity (Hotels; Attractions; Vacation Ownership; finance subsidiary) with counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above state-set counts or of any size, depending on the state
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or regulator where the state requires it

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above state-set counts
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies

obligation: State third-party agent duties (outbound to owners)
trigger: A breach of a system the Hotels division maintains for managed hotel owners
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Owners whose guests' data it is, so they can give their notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel decides when the division acts as an agent for an owner

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents: name with an identity document number, a financial account or card number with any required security code, access code, or password, biometric data, or geolocation (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days on good cause if the Department is told in writing within the 30 days
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - identity document numbers (about 118,000 Floridians); counsel decides for bank account numbers (about 64,000) and card data
notifying_entity: Hotels; Attractions; Vacation Ownership; finance subsidiary

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals, never to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent: inbound from the legacy POS vendor; outbound where the division maintains personal information for owners
deadline: No later than 10 days after the agent determines the breach or has reason to believe it occurred
notify: Inbound: the vendor notifies the group. Outbound: the division notifies each owner
notifying_entity: Group General Counsel; Hotels senior vice president of owner relations

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: For the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Kids' club or biometric data involved
citation: 16 CFR Part 312 (no breach notice rule); Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI)
trigger: Children's information or gate templates are accessed
deadline: No COPPA-specific notice clock; state breach laws apply to biometric data and to parents' account credentials
notify: Parents and passholders under state law
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario (the kids' club store and the gate vendor were not reached); checked on Day 2

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: A cybersecurity incident is discovered
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
notify: Disclosure committee (internal decision recorded with date and reasoning)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: The group determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a written U.S. Attorney General determination)
notify: SEC (public filing to investors)

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the Form 10-K
notify: SEC (risk management, strategy, and governance disclosure)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - lessons from the incident may inform it

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Workforce learn of a potential material cybersecurity incident
deadline: Immediately on knowledge
notify: Disclosure committee members, responders, and executives with knowledge

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering an extortion payment for stolen guest or owner data
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
trigger: Suspected card compromise
deadline: As soon as practical
notify: U.S. Secret Service (as named in the Visa document); FBI field office or IC3

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). The proposed size criterion would cover the group if the rule is finalized as proposed

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (call the carrier hotline before hiring vendors, except a Visa-required PFI)
notify: Carrier breach hotline

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services, or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts
